elhag-dataset-toptagging-2000-images: Sec III.E.1 p.7 and III.E.2 p.8 state the TopTagging dataset, Monte Carlo origin, 2,000 images at 28x28 and the 80/20 split.
elhag-pca-28x28-to-2x2: Sec III.E.3 p.8 states PCA from 28x28 to 2x2, 4 pixels as inputs; p.6 states one pixel per qubit.
elhag-simulator-and-frameworks: Intro p.2 states a classical noiseless simulator (PennyLane) and TensorFlow; Sec IV p.8 names default.qubit. No hardware use follows from the simulator statement.
elhag-proof-of-principle-stage: Intro p.2 states the study is a proof of principle and limited to the hadronic channel of the TopTagging dataset.
elhag-parameter-matching-lr: Sec IV p.8 gives 30 vs 33 and 48 vs 51 parameters and learning rate 0.001 with random init; Sec III.B p.4 gives Adam.
elhag-cnn-architecture-33-params: Sec III.A p.4 states the layers, four feature-map kernels and 33 trainable parameters.
elhag-conv-pool-circuit-gate-counts: Sec III.C.2 p.5 states the gate counts of the SO(4), SU(4) and pooling circuits as the paper's own circuit blocks.
elhag-four-encodings-defined: Sec III.C.1 p.5 names TPE, HEE with 1 and 2 layers (HEE1, HEE2) and CHE with 1 layer as the encodings it uses.
elhag-accuracy-definition-qualitative: Sec IV p.8-9 defines accuracy as correct classifications over total samples and calls the comparison qualitative.
elhag-convergence-not-training-time: Sec IV.B p.10 states the caveat on its own batch-size convergence results. True type is a stated limit on a measured result (F135).
elhag-comparison-not-one-to-one: Conclusion p.12 states that accuracy depends on dataset and preprocessing and that a one-to-one comparison is not possible. A limit on its own comparison.
elhag-classical-cnn-small-params-caveat: Conclusion p.12 states the system was simple so the CNN had very few parameters, unlike usual CNNs.
elhag-code-public: Code Availability p.13 states the code for preprocessing, models and training is available at a GitHub URL with scripts and documentation.
noiseless-simulation-only: Conclusion p.12 states only noiseless simulation was performed and noise would spoil QCNN performance unless tamed.
simple-system-not-general-claim: Conclusion p.12 states the system was relatively simple for both QCNN and CNN and that the authors do not claim to outperform all existing models.
elor-definition-proper-metric: Sec 2 p.2 defines a proper probability metric and states that properness is not defined for label metrics, for which consistency is used.
elor-definition-consistency: Sec 2 p.2 gives the paper's own working description ('roughly speaking') of consistency with respect to a metric.
elor-dataset-sources: Sec 3.1 p.2 states the 104 datasets of [21] and 24 imbalanced-learn datasets not in [21].
elor-removed-48-saturated-datasets: Sec 3.1 p.2 states the removal of 48 saturated datasets (19 at score 1, 29 above 0.99) and the reason.
elor-removed-7-datasets-technical: Sec 3.1 p.2 lists the 7 removed: three with under 8 minority samples, one not found, one with baseline 0, two where SVM-SMOTE failed. Counts add to 7.
elor-oversamplers-list: Sec 3.3 p.3 lists the five oversamplers and why Polynomfit SMOTE was chosen.
elor-classifiers-list-sota: Sec 3.4 p.3 lists the seven classifiers, three called SOTA boosted forests, and four HP configurations each (Table 1).
elor-metrics-and-thresholds: Sec 3.5 p.3 lists the proper probability metrics, label metrics, fixed 0.5 threshold and the threshold optimized on the validation fold.
elor-hp-definitions-apriori-validation: Sec 3.6 p.3 defines a-priori HPs and validation HPs and states the minority ratios 0.1 to 0.5.
elor-experiment-protocol-60-20-20-seven-: Sec 3.7 p.3-4 states the stratified 60/20/20 split, oversampling of the training fold only and seven repeats with different seeds and splits.
elor-open-problem-weak-strong-disparity: Sec 4.2 p.4 leaves the weak/strong disparity unexplained for future work; Conclusion p.6 names the further research direction.
emami-cvqboost-formulation-quadratic: Sec 2.2 p.3-4 states the regularized squared-error objective (eq. 4) and the J and C mapping (eqs. 5, 6), which expand correctly up to a constant. The paper's own formulation.
emami-dirac3-continuous-quadratic-mode: Sec 2.1 p.3 states the continuous quadratic mode (eqs. 1-2) and that higher-order coupling is not used. Describes the mode used, not a performance claim.
emami-weak-classifiers-logistic-regressi: Sec 2.3 p.4 states the four classifier types tested, one or two features each, and logistic regression used.
emami-explainability-not-examined: Sec 2.3 p.4 states the authors elected not to examine explainability, focusing on performance.
emami-dataset-kaggle-size-and-fraud-rate: Sec 2.4 p.4 describes the dataset used as the authors state it. The figures are the paper's description of a third-party dataset and are approximate; the value is attributed to the authors.
emami-dataset-38-features: Sec 2.4 p.4 states 38 features; Tables 2 to 5 repeat 38 features.
emami-balancing-protocol-ratios-auc: Sec 3.1 p.5 states the four strategies on training data only, unchanged test data, six ratios and AUC on test data.
emami-statistics-10-runs-two-sd: Sec 3 p.4-5 states averaging over 10 runs and two-standard-deviation error bars unless stated otherwise.
emami-synthetic-scaling-setup: Sec 3.4 p.9 states make_classification, 1M to 70M samples, 80% training, 100 to 900 features, 48 CPU cores at 2.64 GHz, four L4 GPUs of 24GB and RAPIDS. Setup only, no result.
emami-code-public-vendor-repo: Acknowledgments p.12 states the authors created a code repository for transparency and reproducibility at a GitHub URL under the qci-github organization.
favorable-dirac3-papers-are-qci-authored: Title page p.1 lists all six authors at QCi; Acknowledgments p.12 states all authors were completely supported by QCi. No share or option statement appears in this paper, and the narrowed value says so. The stored value's other claims belong to other records.

theory_low.elor-theorem1-auc-is-proper: Theorem 1 is stated with its i.i.d. condition (Sec 2.1 p.2), but its proof is a direct corollary of Theorem 7 of reference [5] (Lemma 2), a specific other paper's theorem used as the step. Not a self-contained proof.
theory_low.elor-proof-theorem1-two-phase-corollary: The two-phase argument (Sec 2.1 p.2) is short, but it rests on Theorem 7 of [5], restated as Lemma 2 and not proved here. The result depends on a cited theorem.
